title: Menachem, Son of Rabbi Yehudah ben Levi

paragraphs: Menachem son of Rabbi Yehuda ben Levi.

Jerusalem Talmud Demai 5:8 relates that Abba Antoli bought produce from a gentile and went to Rabbi Yehudah ben Levi. He sent word to his son Menachem to arrange its tithing, and the tithe was given. On the return, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi encountered him and asked, “Who would do this but your father?” etc.

notes.text: The gift and return clauses have ambiguous pronouns. The same primary paragraph records an alternative version of Yehoshua ben Levi’s remark. The recipients, returnee and relation between the named Yehudah and Yehoshua are not reconstructed here; the supplied patronym remains unchanged.

The saved whole Venice Demai 5:8 scalar explicitly has Abba Antoli, Rabbi Yehudah ben Levi, his son Menachem, the tithe gift and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's remark, followed by a different version of that remark. This supports these exact full personal titles and the narrative location. Giver, recipient and returnee are not reconstructed from the pronouns, and Yehudah is not silently changed to Yehoshua. The source's כי אתא differs from Venice מי אתי; no print-history claim follows. The alternative remark remains in the evidence rather than being imported into Hyman's abbreviated quotation.

Hyman’s print has Yehudah ben Levi in the first part and Yehoshua ben Levi in the encounter, as do the consulted Jerusalem Talmud texts. Guggenheimer takes Abba Antoli as giving the tithe to Menachem. Penei Moshe takes Menachem as the returnee and, in explaining the alternative version, says Abba gave him the tithe to bring to his father. Penei Moshe calls Yehudah the brother of Yehoshua. Guggenheimer reads “ben Levi” as indicating Levite status and takes the story to imply no further relationship between the two men.
